slice.question: Can public Git commit metadata provide scheduled Chat with a text-native append-only checkpoint lineage sufficient for replay and duplicate/stale-conflict detection without hosted execution, finite optional quota, incremental cost, or manual user execution?
slice.signature_observation: Both sampled commits were reported verified=true by GitHub, but signature verification is provider-reported evidence and is not assumed for all commits.
slice.mechanism: Persist each checkpoint as or bind it to an exact Git commit SHA plus tree SHA and explicit predecessor commit SHA. Replay fetches the exact commit/tree by SHA; duplicate detection compares commit identity; stale/conflicting updates are rejected when the proposed predecessor is not the expected current predecessor. For strict linear CAS semantics, use a single-parent role-local branch/record or explicitly reject merge ambiguity.
what_is_proven: The sampled public commit exposes an exact commit SHA, tree SHA and parent SHA list through lightweight repository metadata.
A directly fetched listed parent exists with its own distinct tree SHA and parent list, giving a replayable predecessor edge without executing repository code.
Exact predecessor equality supplies a text-native stale/conflict check, and exact commit identity supplies duplicate detection, if the checkpoint protocol requires an expected predecessor.

The mechanism uses repository transport only; it does not require Actions, hosted runners, Codespaces, artifacts/LFS/packages, external verifier execution, paid/trial monthly credits, or manual user execution for the tested metadata outcome.
limits_and_counterexamples: Git history is a DAG, not inherently a single append-only chain; merge commits have multiple parents. A strict checkpoint CAS protocol must restrict to single-parent updates or define an explicit chosen predecessor.
A mutable branch ref can be force-pushed. Commit SHA lineage detects that a fetched candidate does not descend from the expected predecessor, but it does not make the provider ref itself append-only.
Provider availability/retention is trusted: unreachable objects may not remain fetchable forever, so this is not a provider-independent archival ledger.

A GitHub-reported verified signature strengthens provider-anchored provenance for sampled commits but does not establish provider-independent authenticity, universal signing, or external key-policy verification.

Test whether provider-signed commits or signed tags can add useful provenance without requiring external verifier execution, finite quota, incremental cost, or manual user execution.
Keep provider-independent append-only retention and force-push resistance unresolved until separately tested.
